Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Solutions Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Sarah Miller, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Miller, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to InnovaTech Solutions’ Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alan Johnson, CEO; David Chen, CFO; and Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Alan.

Alan Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Sarah. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Okay, let's dive into a detailed analysis of our Q1 performance, specifically focusing on Net Margin and Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS). As the summary indicates, we delivered a solid Q1, exceeding our own expectations for EPS. Let's break down the contributing factors and look at the underlying trends.
In Q1, our Diluted EPS came in at $0.89, representing a 2% increase compared to the $0.87 we reported in Q1 of the prior year. This also translates to a $0.02 beat over our initial guidance of $0.87 per share. While a 2% increase might seem modest on the surface, it's crucial to consider the challenging macroeconomic environment we've been navigating, characterized by inflationary pressures, supply chain volatility, and fluctuating currency exchange rates. Furthermore, this growth was achieved despite making significant investments in our R&D pipeline and our ongoing digital transformation initiatives. Our Net Margin for Q1 stood at 14.5%, slightly below the 15.2% we achieved in Q1 of the previous year. This 70 basis point decline is primarily attributable to two key factors: increased input costs and strategic pricing adjustments in certain key markets. We experienced a noticeable increase in raw material costs, particularly in our "Advanced Materials" division, where the price of rare earth elements used in our battery technology saw a significant surge (approximately a 12% increase year-over-year). This affected our cost of goods sold (COGS), putting downward pressure on our gross margin and consequently, our net margin. In the European market, we implemented targeted price reductions on our "Renewable Energy Solutions" product line to maintain market share in the face of increased competition from lower-cost alternatives. This strategic move, while impacting our net margin in the short term, is expected to drive higher volume sales and long-term customer loyalty, positioning us for sustained growth as the European market recovers. Despite these challenges, we implemented several cost-saving initiatives throughout the quarter that helped mitigate the impact on our net margin. These included successfully negotiating more favorable terms with key suppliers, resulting in a 3% reduction in overall procurement costs, the ongoing investments in automation across our manufacturing facilities which have yielded significant efficiency gains, reducing labor costs by approximately 5%, and consolidating several regional distribution centers, resulting in lower transportation and warehousing expenses. While the overall EPS growth was 2%, the drivers behind this growth varied significantly across different regions. North America remained our strongest performing region, contributing significantly to the overall EPS growth. A 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven primarily by strong demand for our "Cloud Computing Services" and "Cybersecurity Solutions," helped fuel this performance. Our investments in expanding our sales team and strengthening our channel partnerships in this region are clearly paying off. The Asia-Pacific region experienced moderate growth, with revenue up 5% year-over-year. While demand for our products and services remains robust in this region, we faced headwinds from increased competition and currency fluctuations. We are actively exploring new market entry strategies and developing customized solutions to cater to the specific needs of customers in this region. As mentioned earlier, the European market presented challenges due to economic uncertainty and increased competition. While revenue remained relatively flat compared to the prior year, we are confident that our strategic pricing adjustments and investments in building brand awareness will help us regain market share in the coming quarters. Our ongoing investments in R&D and digital transformation are crucial for driving long-term growth and profitability. We are leveraging AI to enhance our product offerings, improve operational efficiency, and personalize customer experiences. For example, we have integrated AI-powered analytics into our "Financial Services" platform, enabling our clients to make more informed investment decisions. We are expanding our cloud computing infrastructure to meet the growing demand for our cloud-based solutions. This includes investing in new data centers and developing innovative cloud-native applications. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and developing sustainable solutions for our customers. We are investing in renewable energy sources, implementing energy-efficient technologies, and promoting sustainable business practices throughout our supply chain. While Q1 presented certain challenges, we remain optimistic about our long-term growth prospects. Our strong market position, diversified product portfolio, and strategic investments in innovation position us well to navigate the evolving market landscape and deliver sustainable value to our shareholders. We are closely monitoring macroeconomic trends and are prepared to adjust our strategies as needed. We are reaffirming our full-year EPS guidance of $3.60 - $3.70 per share, reflecting our confidence in our ability to execute our strategic initiatives and achieve our financial goals. We anticipate seeing net margin improve throughout the remainder of the year as the benefits of our cost-saving initiatives and strategic pricing adjustments materialize. We will continue to prioritize operational efficiency and strategic investments to drive sustainable growth and profitability in the years to come.

We also saw great momentum in Okay, let's break down the revenue guidance and forecasts for the upcoming year and specifically Q2, focusing on the Data-Centric and PC-Centric segments. While the overall picture presents some challenges, we can identify nuances and potential growth pockets within each segment. Our revised full-year revenue outlook of $69 billion, representing a 3% year-over-year decline, reflects a more conservative view of the macroeconomic environment and its impact on enterprise IT spending cycles. This adjustment primarily stems from headwinds in the Data-Centric Group (DCG), partially offset by the relative stability in the PC-Centric segment. Within the data-centric businesses, we anticipate a low single-digit percentage decline overall for the full year. However, this aggregate figure masks significant variations across different product lines. DCG is expected to be down mid-single digits. Specifically, we forecast a decline of approximately 4.5%, resulting in projected full-year revenue of around $31.5 billion compared to $33 billion last year. This decline is largely attributed to delayed enterprise refresh cycles, where enterprises are extending their existing server infrastructure lifecycles due to economic uncertainty. Budget cuts and prioritization of cloud migration initiatives are contributing factors. This delay is particularly noticeable in North America and parts of Europe. We are seeing a slower adoption rate for our newest "Sapphire Rapids" generation of processors than initially anticipated, particularly among smaller and mid-sized businesses. However, larger hyperscale customers remain committed to planned deployments, providing some offset. Increased competition from AMD's continued gains in the server market are putting pressure on our market share and pricing. We are actively responding with competitive product offerings and targeted pricing strategies, but the impact on revenue is undeniable. Geopolitical tensions and regulatory uncertainties in China are impacting DCG revenue. We're seeing a shift towards domestic suppliers by some customers, impacting our overall market share in the region. We anticipate further impacts from ongoing trade restrictions, specifically relating to advanced AI chips. Despite significant price erosion in the NAND flash memory market, we anticipate a slight increase in bit shipments, driven by demand from cloud storage providers and the growing adoption of SSDs in PCs. However, the lower average selling prices (ASPs) will largely offset the volume increase, leading to flat to slightly negative revenue growth in this area for the full year. We are forecasting approximately $6.7 billion in revenue for NAND, up 1% year over year. Strategic initiatives to focus on higher-margin enterprise SSDs and QLC (Quad-Level Cell) technology are expected to improve profitability in the long term. The networking segment, which includes Ethernet controllers, switches, and related technologies, is expected to perform relatively well, driven by the continued expansion of cloud infrastructure and the increasing demand for high-bandwidth connectivity. We project $3.5 billion in revenue, up 3% year over year. Our investments in innovative technologies like Silicon Photonics are expected to drive long-term growth in this segment. The PC-centric segment forecast remains unchanged at a low single-digit decline for the full year. We anticipate a 2% decline resulting in a full-year revenue estimate of $33.3 billion. This reflects the continued softness in the consumer PC market, partially offset by demand for commercial PCs. We are seeing continued strength in the commercial PC market, driven by the need for upgrades to support hybrid work environments and the adoption of Windows 11. Our vPro platform continues to be a key differentiator, offering enhanced security and manageability features that are highly valued by enterprise customers. We expect commercial PC revenue to be approximately flat year-over-year. The consumer PC market remains challenging, with demand still below pre-pandemic levels. Inflation and economic uncertainty are impacting consumer spending, leading to longer replacement cycles. While we anticipate a rebound in the second half of the year as economic conditions improve and new product launches stimulate demand, the overall outlook remains cautious. We are projecting a low single-digit decline in consumer PC revenue for the full year. The second quarter is expected to be a particularly challenging period, with revenue projected to be $15.6 billion, representing an 8% year-over-year decline. This reflects the continued headwinds in both the Data-Centric and PC-Centric segments. Specifically, we expect the data-centric businesses to decline in the high single digits, approximately 8.5% year-over-year, resulting in a projected revenue of approximately $7.1 billion. We anticipate DCG to be the primary driver of the decline, with a projected decrease of around 9%, resulting in revenue of approximately $6 billion. This reflects the delayed enterprise refresh cycles discussed earlier, as well as the impact of increased competition and China market challenges. We are implementing aggressive cost-cutting measures to mitigate the impact on profitability. We expect NAND to be down approximately 5% in Q2, reflecting the challenging pricing environment. We are expecting a modest 2% increase in the networking segment for Q2, driven by continued demand from cloud providers. The PC-centric segment is also expected to decline in the high single digits, approximately 7.5% year-over-year, resulting in a projected revenue of approximately $8.5 billion. This reflects the continued weakness in the consumer PC market, partially offset by strength in the commercial PC segment. Commercial PC sales in Q2 are relatively strong, but not enough to offset overall segment softness. Consumer PC sales in Q2 remain significantly below last year's levels, impacting revenue. Despite the near-term challenges, we remain confident in our long-term growth prospects. We are actively pursuing several strategic initiatives to drive future growth, including accelerating the development and launch of next-generation products, expanding our presence in high-growth markets such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and edge computing, improving our operational efficiency, and building stronger relationships with our customers. We believe that these strategic initiatives will enable us to navigate the current challenges and drive long-term growth and profitability. While the short-term outlook is uncertain, we remain optimistic about the future of our company and our ability to deliver value to our shareholders. We anticipate a gradual improvement in the second half of the year as economic conditions stabilize and demand for our products rebounds. We will continue to monitor the situation closely and adjust our plans as needed. We are seeing the brunt of the enterprise spending slowdown in North America, and Europe is similar to North America, with added complexity due to energy crisis. Asia-Pacific is showing mixed performance. China is facing challenges, while other regions like Southeast Asia show pockets of growth. Latin America is relatively resilient, but smaller market impact overall.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to David to walk through in more detail.

While our Q2 results highlighted a slight contraction in operating margin due to specific factors, our Q3 guidance reflects proactive measures to mitigate these challenges while strategically investing in key growth areas. This reduction is primarily attributable to a temporary softening in demand from our Tier 2 smartphone OEM partners in emerging markets, specifically in the Southeast Asia region. These OEMs are facing increased price sensitivity from consumers due to inflationary pressures, leading to a temporary slowdown in adoption of our premium platform solutions. We expect this pressure to alleviate as the macroeconomic situation improves and as we introduce more cost-effective platform variants tailored to their needs in Q4. The ramp-up of our new generation 4G modem, the XG450, is progressing according to plan. We anticipate revenue from this segment to reach approximately $450 million, a significant increase of 30% compared to Q2. This increase is driven by strong demand from automotive and IoT applications, where the XG450's enhanced power efficiency and connectivity features are proving particularly attractive. We are actively working to diversify our 4G modem customer base and expand into new industry verticals to further solidify our leadership in this space. Our Q1 2024 operating margin landed at 28.0%, a figure that, while still robust, reflects a decrease of 200 basis points (2.0 percentage points) compared to the 30.0% achieved in Q4 2023. It's also down 150 basis points (1.5 percentage points) from the 29.5% reported in Q1 2023. This performance requires a nuanced understanding of the underlying drivers, which are a mix of strategic investments, market dynamics, and specific operational factors. The primary drivers for the QoQ decline can be attributed to the significant acceleration in the production ramp of our next-generation 10-nanometer processors. While we are excited about the performance and power efficiency benefits these chips offer, the initial phase of mass production is inherently associated with higher manufacturing costs. Specifically, we saw increased depreciation expenses related to new equipment, higher material costs due to initial yield curves, and elevated engineering costs associated with optimizing the production process. We estimate that these factors collectively reduced our operating margin by approximately 130 basis points. An example, the depreciation of our new fabrication plant in Arizona alone accounted for a 40 basis point reduction. The cyclical nature of the NAND flash memory market presented a headwind this quarter. Following a period of strong demand and pricing in late 2023, we observed a softening in the market in Q1 2024, driven by increased supply and moderating demand in the consumer electronics segment. In anticipation of potential price declines, we proactively increased our NAND reserves by $75 million. This conservative accounting practice, while prudent in the long run, negatively impacted our Q1 operating margin by approximately 90 basis points. This was most prominent in our Storage Solutions Group (SSG), with a 12% decrease in average selling price (ASP) for our enterprise SSDs. Partially offsetting these negative factors was a significant increase in the average selling price (ASP) of our platform solutions, particularly within the Client Computing Group (CCG). This increase was driven by a combination of factors. Firstly, continued supply chain constraints at the lower end of the CCG product stack led to a richer product mix, with a higher proportion of premium, higher-margin processors being sold. Secondly, strong demand for our high-performance gaming and workstation processors, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region (APAC), further contributed to the ASP increase. We estimate that this favorable product mix and strong demand added approximately 50 basis points to our operating margin. For example, our Core i9 series saw a 22% increase in unit sales, contributing significantly to the higher ASP. We achieved efficiencies in our operating expenses by rigorously managing discretionary spending across the organization. We saw a reduction in travel and marketing expenses, as well as a slowdown in hiring for non-critical roles. We estimate these reductions in spending contributed positively to operating margin by around 50 basis points. The year-over-year decline of 1.5 percentage points can be explained by our significantly increased our R&D spending in Q1 2024, particularly in areas such as AI accelerators, advanced packaging technologies, and next-generation process nodes (beyond 10nm). This reflects our commitment to long-term innovation and maintaining our competitive edge. While these investments are crucial for our future growth, they had a negative impact of approximately 100 basis points on our Q1 operating margin. Specifically, our AI-related R&D spend increased by 35% YoY. Increased competition in the CPU market, particularly from AMD's Ryzen series, resulted in some pricing pressure. To maintain market share, we implemented targeted price reductions in certain segments, which negatively impacted our operating margin by approximately 70 basis points. Similar to the QoQ changes, platform ASP strength (driven by supply constraints and product mix) and lower spending overall partially offset these negative factors. In our Q4 2023 earnings call, we provided guidance for a Q1 2024 operating margin of 29.0%. Our actual result of 28.0% represents a miss of 100 basis points. This variance is primarily attributable to a higher-than-expected NAND Reserve. While we anticipated some softening in the NAND market, the magnitude of the price decline exceeded our initial projections. This required us to increase our NAND reserves by an additional $30 million beyond what was factored into our guidance, resulting in a larger-than-expected negative impact on our operating margin. We had projected the NAND reserve impact to be around 60 basis points, but it ended up being 90 basis points. The initial prediction was based on industry analysts forecasts from December, but the actual market conditions shifted significantly throughout January. Unforeseen Supply Chain Disruptions also played a role. While we had anticipated supply chain constraints in the low-end CCG segment, a new disruption emerged related to a key component supplier in Malaysia following a major weather event. This further exacerbated the supply issues and contributed to the higher ASP strength but also brought added costs associated with expedited shipping and alternative sourcing. These costs were not fully accounted for in our original guidance. While the Q1 operating margin fell slightly below expectations, we remain confident in our long-term financial outlook. We are actively addressing the identified challenges through the following initiatives, including 10nm Yield Improvement, NAND Market Management, R&D Efficiency, and Cost Optimization. We believe that these actions will enable us to improve our operating margin in the coming quarters and deliver strong financial performance for the full year. We remain committed to our long-term strategic goals and confident in our ability to create value for our shareholders.

The networking area, which includes our Ethernet controllers and programmable switches, saw a more modest decline of 4%. Growth in demand from telecom operators for 5G infrastructure was partially offset by slower spending on enterprise networking upgrades. DCG's gross margin of 42% represents a 300 basis point decline compared to Q3 2023. This was primarily due to a less favorable product mix, with a higher proportion of revenue coming from lower-margin cloud custom CPUs, as well as increased pricing pressure in the general-purpose server market. We are actively working to improve margins through cost optimization initiatives and a shift towards higher-value, differentiated products. While DCG's Q3 performance was below our expectations, we remain confident in the long-term growth potential of this market. We are seeing strong customer interest in our next-generation Sapphire Rapids processors, which will begin shipping in volume in Q4. These processors offer significant performance and efficiency improvements, and we believe they will enable us to regain market share in the server space. Furthermore, we are doubling down on our AI strategy within DCG, focusing on providing a comprehensive portfolio of hardware and software solutions for AI workloads. Our Gaudi AI accelerators are gaining traction, and we expect to see significant revenue growth in this area in the coming quarters. CCG delivered a solid performance in Q3, with revenue increasing 4% year-over-year to $9.1 billion. This growth was primarily driven by strong demand for our mobile processors, particularly in the high-end gaming and creator segments. Revenue from mobile processors increased 8% year-over-year, driven by successful product launches and a rebound in the premium laptop market. Our 13th Gen Intel Core mobile processors, featuring innovative power management and integrated graphics, have been well-received by both consumers and OEMs. Desktop revenue declined 2% year-over-year. While demand for high-end gaming desktops remained strong, the overall desktop market continues to face secular headwinds as users increasingly shift to laptops and other mobile devices. Revenue from ChromeOS devices saw an impressive 15% increase in Q3, reflecting continued strong demand in the education sector and growing adoption in the enterprise market. Our collaboration with Google on optimized processors for ChromeOS continues to yield positive results. CCG's gross margin of 36% was flat compared to Q3 2023.
